target.title: Discriminative Multi-modality Speech Recognition
target.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2020, pp. 14433-14442
target.version: CVPR 2020 paper (CVF Open Access), same text as arXiv:2005.05592v1 (first public 2020-05-12); wiki folders cvf-xu20-aemsr and cvf-xu20-msr hold the same PDF (sha256 f082a81a...)

read.pdf: Text-extracted Fig. 1-4 captions/labels and Tables 1-4 captions/rows; all 49 references

entries.text: The proposed AE-MSR uses visual lip information first to enhance target audio and then fuses enhanced audio with video again for speech recognition (double visual awareness).
entries.condition: Two-stage audio-enhancement then audio-visual recognition architecture.
entries.quote: The goal of this paper is to introduce a two-stage speech recognition method with double visual-modality awareness.

entries.text: Novelty claim: unlike prior MSR systems using visual awareness once, AE-MSR uses lip video to filter competing voices/background noise before a second visual-audio fusion for recognition.
entries.condition: Authors describe this as the first visual-awareness pass; then video is combined again at MSR.

entries.text: Authors claim the P3D visual front-end extracts more discriminative video features than the C3D-2D-ResNet front-end used by Afouras et al. [2].
entries.condition: Qualitative architecture comparison; LRW word accuracy is reported separately in Table 1.
entries.quote: We introduce the P3D as visual front-end to extract more discriminative visual features

entries.text: Authors replace 1D-ResNet temporal blocks with TCN blocks in AE to establish longer temporal connections; Table 3 and Table 4 compare the alternatives.
entries.condition: TCN and 1D-ResNet variants are evaluated within the AE sub-network.
entries.quote: We upgrade the temporal convolution block of 1D ResNet to a TCN one in AE sub-network for estab- lishing temporal connections.

entries.text: Authors claim EleAtt-GRU is more effective than Transformer for long sequences and report lower WER for EG-seq2seq than TM-seq2seq in their comparisons.
entries.condition: The paper attributes the difference to the transformer's limited character-relationship length; no statistical significance analysis is reported.

entries.text: The authors claim AE-MSR surpasses the state-of-the-art MSR model on LRS3-TED in clean and noisy audio conditions.
entries.condition: Authors identify [2] as the state-of-the-art MSR comparator; WER comparisons appear in Tables 2-3.

entries.text: The authors claim their P3D-based word-classification model exceeds the prior LRW word-level state of the art [41].
entries.condition: LRW, 500-word classification; reported word accuracy is in Table 1.

entries.text: The authors acknowledge that audio-only EG-seq2seq and TM-seq2seq cease to work at -10 dB SNR.
entries.condition: LRS3-TED; audio modality only; Table 2; no language model in decoder for the reported comparison.

entries.text: The authors report that multimodal recognition sometimes fails in noisy conditions even when enhanced-audio prediction succeeds; the paper gives qualitative examples, not a failure rate.
entries.condition: Qualitative supplementary examples; no count or denominator reported.

entries.text: Audio input is sampled at 16 kHz; STFT uses a 40 ms window and 10 ms hop (75% overlap), then an 80-bin mel-spaced filter from 0 to 8 kHz.
entries.unit: audio sampling rate; STFT window/hop; overlap; mel bins/frequency range
entries.condition: Audio feature extraction for AE-MSR; video frame rate is 25 fps.

entries.text: The visual ROI is a mouth patch cropped from original video frames at 112 by 112 pixels; video frame rate is 25 fps.
entries.condition: Input to C3D-P3D visual front-end; paper does not state pixel-value normalization.

entries.text: The C3D-P3D visual front-end begins with a 3D convolution of 64 filters and kernel 5 x 7 x 7, followed by BN, ReLU and max-pooling.
entries.condition: Visual front-end before the 50-layer P3D ResNet.

entries.text: P3D ResNet factorizes N x N x N convolutions into 1 x 3 x 3 spatial and 3 x 1 x 1 temporal filters; the implemented network has 50 layers and emits T x 512 features.
entries.value: N x N x N; 1 x 3 x 3; 3 x 1 x 1; 50 layers; T x 512
entries.condition: The P3D front-end maintains the temporal dimension T while reducing spatial dimensions.

entries.text: AE fuses video and noisy-magnitude features; two intermediate temporal-convolution blocks upsample video features by 4 to match audio length 4T. MSR later downsamples enhanced-audio time by 4 to match video length T.
entries.value: 4T in AE; factor 4 downsampling in MSR
entries.condition: AE includes Nv video and Na audio temporal-convolution blocks; Nv and Na are not numerically specified in the main text.

entries.text: AE predicts a target enhancement mask with values in [0,1] and multiplies it element-wise by the original noisy magnitude spectrogram.
entries.condition: The enhancement target is magnitude spectrogram, not a waveform estimate.

entries.text: The MSR network uses two-layer EleAtt-GRU encoders for both modalities; each EleAtt-GRU unit count is 128. Enhanced audio passes through two stride-2 1D-ResNet blocks to downsample time by 4.
entries.value: 2 encoder layers per modality; 128 units; 2 stride-2 blocks; factor 4 downsampling
entries.condition: Audio and video contexts are separately decoded and then concatenated for character prediction.

entries.text: Decoder vocabulary has 41 output symbols: 26 alphabet characters, 10 digits, and [PAD], [EOS], [BOS], [SPACE].
entries.condition: Character-level decoder; special tokens are padding, end-of-sequence, beginning-of-sequence, and space.
entries.quote: Output size of decoder is set to 41, accounting for the 26 characters in the alphabet, the 10 dig- its, and tokens for [PAD], [EOS], [BOS] and [SPACE].

entries.text: LRW is used to pre-train the P3D visual front-end on a 500-class word-level lip-reading classification task; the front-end is then frozen while features and spectrograms are extracted.
entries.condition: Two-step front-end training; cross-entropy classification; frozen features for downstream AE/MSR training.
entries.quote: We use LRW dataset to pre-train the P3D spatio-temporal front-end based on a word-level classiﬁcation network of lip reading.

entries.text: LRW is described as up to 1,000 utterances for each of 500 different words, spoken by more than 1,000 speakers.
entries.value: up to 1,000 utterances; 500 words; more than 1,000 speakers
entries.condition: Dataset description; the paper does not report the exact subset or subject count used for Table 1.

entries.text: LRS3-TED is described as face tracks from over 400 hours of TED/TEDx videos, split into pre-train, train-val, and test sets.
entries.condition: AE and MSR are trained on LRS3-TED; reported sentence WER uses the dataset, but the specific partition is not named alongside results.

entries.text: Training babble noise is mixed into the audio with probability 0.25 at SNRs from -10 to 10 dB; noise samples are mixtures of 30 LRS3-TED audio samples.
entries.unit: SNR; probability; audio samples per babble mixture
entries.condition: Stated training augmentation. The test-time noise recipe and any overlap with training noise samples are not specified.
entries.quote: with SNR from -10 dB to 10 dB is added to audio stream with probabil- ity pn = 0.25

entries.text: Babble noise samples are synthesized by mixing 30 different audio samples from LRS3-TED.
entries.condition: Training noise construction; no test-time noise sample selection procedure is supplied.
entries.quote: the babble noise samples are synthesized by mixing the signals of 30 different audio samples from LRS3-TED dataset

entries.text: Sentence recognition is scored with WER = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference word count; LRW is scored by word-classification accuracy.
entries.condition: WER reference normalization, case/punctuation handling, and tokenization are not described.

entries.text: AE is trained with L1 loss between predicted and ground-truth magnitude spectrograms; MSR uses sequence-to-sequence loss, with cross-entropy on character outputs.
entries.condition: MSR also trains with audio-only or visual-only input; AE and MSR training stages are described separately.
entries.quote: The AE sub-network is trained by minimizing the L1 loss between the predicted magnitude spectrogram and the ground truth.

entries.text: The visual front-end is trained in two steps: 3D convolution plus 50-layer P3D and a dense layer, then the dense layer is replaced by two Bi-LSTM layers followed by linear and SoftMax layers.
entries.value: 2 training steps; 50 P3D layers; 2 Bi-LSTM layers
entries.condition: LRW, 500 word classes; cross-entropy loss; no epochs or batch size stated.

entries.text: AE sub-networks are trained separately with TCN and 1D-ResNet blocks; AE-MSR then freezes AE and trains the combined network. Training begins with one-word sequences whose length gradually increases.
entries.value: one-word starting sequence; progressively increasing sequence length
entries.condition: No exact sequence-length schedule, epoch count, or stopping rule is reported.

entries.text: Training uses Adam, dropout, and label smoothing; the initial learning rate is 1e-4, halved when training error does not improve, with final rate 5e-6.
entries.condition: No dropout rate, label-smoothing value, patience, optimizer beta values, epoch count, or batch size is provided.

entries.text: Implementation uses TensorFlow and one Tesla P100 GPU with 16 GB memory; reported full training duration is approximately 15 days.
entries.unit: GPU count; memory; elapsed training time
entries.condition: Includes AE variants, MSR training, and subsequent joint training; hardware/software versions and total run repetitions are not stated.

entries.condition: LRW, word-level classification over 500 classes; Table 1 does not identify the evaluated split or exact test sample count.

questions.q: Is word-boundary use stated for the LRW classifier?
questions.answer: No; boundaries are not mentioned anywhere in the text (searched).

questions.q: Which TM-seq2seq cells in Tables 2-3 coincide with Afouras et al. Table 2 no-LM values?
questions.answer: Clean A 9.0, V 59.9, AV 8.0; 0 dB A 60.5, AV 44.3; Google 10.4 and 70.3.

questions.q: Is the MSR sub-network trained on noisy audio?
questions.answer: Sec. 4.3 says MSR is trained with video features and clean magnitude spectrograms; the babble augmentation paragraph does not say which sub-network it applies to.
